   150	/// of the screen.
   151	///
   152	/// This property is useful for renderers which want to copy just the pages
   153	/// for the visible portion of the screen, or for infinite scrollback where
   154	/// we may want to serialize and store pages that are sufficiently far
   155	/// away from the current viewport.
   156	///
   157	/// Pages are always backed by a single contiguous block of memory that is
   158	/// aligned on a page boundary. This makes it easy and fast to copy pages
   159	/// around. Within the contiguous block of memory, the contents of a page are
   160	/// thoughtfully laid out to optimize primarily for terminal IO (VT streams)
   161	/// and to minimize memory usage.
   162	pub const Page = struct {
   163	    comptime {
   164	        // The alignment of our members. We want to ensure that the page
   165	        // alignment is always divisible by this.
   166	        assert(std.heap.page_size_min % @max(
   167	            @alignOf(Row),
   168	            cells_align,
   169	            MetaLayout.alignment,
   170	        ) == 0);
   171	    }
   172	
   173	    /// The backing memory for the page. A page is always made up of a
   174	    /// a single contiguous block of memory that is aligned on a page
   175	    /// boundary and is a multiple of the system page size.
   176	    memory: []align(std.heap.page_size_min) u8,
   177	
   178	    /// The array of rows in the page. The rows are always in row order
   179	    /// (i.e. index 0 is the top row, index 1 is the row below that, etc.)
   180	    rows: Offset(Row),
   181	
   182	    /// The array of cells in the page. The cells are NOT in row order,
   183	    /// but they are in column order. To determine the mapping of cells
   184	    /// to row, you must use the `rows` field. From the pointer to the
   185	    /// first column, all cells in that row are laid out in column order.
   186	    cells: Offset(Cell),
   187	
   188	    /// Set to true when an operation is performed that dirties all rows in
   189	    /// the page. See `Row.dirty` for more information on dirty tracking.
   190	    ///
   191	    /// NOTE: A value of false does NOT indicate that
   192	    ///       the page has no dirty rows in it, only
   193	    ///       that no full-page-dirtying operations
   194	    ///       have occurred since it was last cleared.
   195	    dirty: bool,
   196	
   197	    /// The string allocator for this page used for shared utf-8 encoded
   198	    /// strings. Liveness of strings and memory management is deferred to
   199	    /// the individual use case.
   200	    string_alloc: StringAlloc,
   201	
   202	    /// The multi-codepoint grapheme data for this page. This is where
   203	    /// any cell that has more than one codepoint will be stored. This is
   204	    /// relatively rare (typically only emoji) so this defaults to a very small
   205	    /// size and we force page realloc when it grows.
   206	    grapheme_alloc: GraphemeAlloc,
   207

   209	    /// cell offset to the grapheme data offset. Therefore, whenever a

  5274	/// PageList-owned state for incremental compression.
  5275	///
  5276	/// The position is stored as a page serial rather than a node pointer so it
  5277	/// remains safe when PageList operations destroy, replace, or reuse nodes
  5278	/// between steps. It also records the first serial which was unallocated at
  5279	/// the prior step so new nodes before a valid marker restart safely. If the
  5280	/// exact serial no longer exists in the cold prefix, the next step also
  5281	/// restarts at the first page.
  5282	///
  5283	/// A completed pass is followed by another pass from the oldest cold page.
  5284	/// Compression becomes idle only when that verification pass compresses no
  5285	/// pages. This converges after pages are restored between incremental steps
  5286	/// without requiring consumers to maintain a separate attempt cursor.

  5288	    flags: packed struct {
  5289	        /// Set after any page is compressed during the current traversal.
  5290	        /// We always run incremental compression until we get a fully
  5291	        /// no-compression pass (the verification pass). This lets us
  5292	        /// recompress decompressed pages due to search, scrolling, etc.
  5293	        did_compress: bool = false,
  5294	
  5295	        /// Set after a traversal first reaches the active boundary. When this
  5296	        /// verification traversal reaches the boundary, `did_compress`
  5297	        /// determines whether to restart once more or finish the pass.
  5298	        verifying: bool = false,
  5299	    } = .{},

  5301	    /// Changes whenever PageList activity may affect compression work.
  5302	    /// Callers use this value (via Terminal.compressionActivity) to
  5303	    /// determine whether to recompress.
  5304	    ///
  5305	    /// The directionality of this doesn't matter. We overflow and
  5306	    /// wrap when maxxed. The comparison of this value to your saved
  5307	    /// value is all that matters. There is a possible edge case where you
  5308	    /// don't compress, a full wraparound happens, and you get the same value,
  5309	    /// but its so unlikely.
  5310	    ///
  5311	    /// This is 48-bits so that 16-bits can be reserved for Terminal to
  5312	    /// add extra state.
  5313	    activity_serial: u48 = 0,
  5314	
  5315	    /// Serial of the last page inspected by the traversal. This is
  5316	    /// intentionally an implementation detail and is reset by PageList
  5317	    /// operations which restart traversal progress.
  5318	    last_serial: ?u64 = null,
  5319	
  5320	    /// First node serial which had not been allocated at the prior step. A
  5321	    /// node at or above this value before the saved marker requires a restart.
  5322	    next_serial: u64 = 0,
  5323	
  5324	    /// Record activity without disturbing valid traversal progress.

  5326	        self.activity_serial +%= 1;
  5327	    }

  5329	    /// Discard traversal progress without changing the activity token.

  5334	};

  5349	/// Iterate complete historical pages which do not intersect the viewport.
  5350	///
  5351	/// All boundaries come from PageList pins and Page metadata. Advancing this
  5352	/// iterator never restores a compressed page or reads its backing memory.
  5353	const CompressionIterator = struct {
  5354	    current: *List.Node,
  5355	    active: *List.Node,
  5356	    viewport_first: *List.Node,
  5357	    viewport_last: *List.Node,
  5358	
  5359	    fn init(self: *const PageList) CompressionIterator {
  5360	        return .{
  5361	            .current = self.pages.first.?,
  5362	            .active = self.getTopLeft(.active).node,
  5363	            .viewport_first = self.getTopLeft(.viewport).node,
  5364	            .viewport_last = self.getBottomRight(.viewport).?.node,
  5365	        };
  5366	    }
  5367	
  5368	    fn next(self: *CompressionIterator) ?*List.Node {
  5369	        while (self.current != self.active) {
  5370	            // The viewport is a contiguous node range. Once traversal reaches
  5371	            // its first node, advance through the complete visible range and
  5372	            // resume at the next offscreen page.
  5373	            if (self.current == self.viewport_first) {
  5374	                while (self.current != self.active and
  5375	                    self.current != self.viewport_last)
  5376	                {
  5377	                    self.current = self.current.next.?;
  5378	                }
  5379	
  5380	                if (self.current == self.active) return null;
  5381	                self.current = self.current.next.?;
  5382	                continue;
  5383	            }
  5384	
  5385	            const node = self.current;
  5386	            self.current = node.next.?;
  5387	            return node;
  5388	        }
  5389	
  5390	        return null;
  5391	    }
  5392	
  5393	    fn done(self: *const CompressionIterator) bool {
  5394	        return self.current == self.active;
  5395	    }
  5396	};
